blocks.name: core
blocks.boundary: Converts text to URL-safe slugs with only lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens; raises TypeError if text is not a string
blocks.shape_driver: Single-function tiny library requirement means monolithic implementation in one module

decomposition: A single block contains the entire public API implementation. The 'tiny library' requirement and single-function surface mean minimal decomposition; all logic for type checking, character filtering, word boundary detection, and slug assembly is unified within the slugify function and any helper functions in slug.py.

rejected.idea: Using a third-party library like python-slugify for slug generation
rejected.why: Dead on the method - the brief explicitly requires no third-party dependencies

rejected.idea: Transliterating non-ASCII characters to ASCII equivalents (e.g., e-acute to e)
rejected.why: Dead on the method - transliteration of non-ASCII characters is explicitly out of scope per the brief

rejected.idea: Providing a command-line interface (CLI) for slug generation
rejected.why: Dead on the method - CLI is explicitly out of scope per the brief

rejected.idea: Using regex patterns for word boundary detection
rejected.why: Dead at this size - for a tiny library, manual string processing is more appropriate than regex overhead

risks: Word boundary detection algorithm undefined; camelCase, underscores, punctuation, and mixed separator handling all unclear, risking unexpected slug output
Multiple consecutive separators behavior unspecified; unclear whether 'hello  world' becomes 'hello-world' or 'hello--world'
Leading and trailing hyphen handling undefined; unclear whether '-hello-' is stripped to 'hello' or preserved
Empty string behavior undefined; slugify('') return value not specified
Special-character-only input behavior undefined; slugify('!!!') return value or exception not specified
not_decided: Algorithm for word boundary detection: which characters/transitions (spaces, punctuation, underscores, camelCase) should be treated as word separators?
Multiple consecutive separator handling: should they collapse into a single hyphen or be preserved?
Leading and trailing hyphen stripping: should leading/trailing hyphens be removed from the final slug?
Empty string behavior: what should slugify('') return?
Special-character-only behavior: what should slugify('!!!') return?
